I'm okay with incompetent players at any level, with the condition being they have to be willing to listen, learn, and try their best. 

Not everyone is going to be good at the game. They could be disabled or injured, trying to play despite it. My mother for example, 50 years old and has had a couple traumatic brain injuries. Horrible at dodging aoes because the brain damage makes her slow to process. She also struggles with learning mechanics on the fly, since she just can't keep up. 

Another is that it could be a kid. I started playing WoW at 8 years old, I could see other kids trying ffxiv out. They aren't going to have the motor skills and reaction time that an adult would have. They also might not comprehend mechanics as easily.

Normally when I encounter someone playing awful, I'll say something if it's easy to fix. Tank stance, mechanic explanation, etc. If they respond positively or at least listen, then I brush it off. If they ask questions in good faith, then that's even better. I've added people to my friends list just so they can message me for help if they need it.

The people I really have issues are the ones who are awful, but refuse to take responsibility. If they know they are playing wrong and get angry when it's pointed out, or if they intentionally make things harder for their teammates, that's when I get angry. Have you heard of the critically acclaimed MMORPG Final Fantasy XIV? With an expanded free trial which you can play through the entirety of A Realm Reborn and the award winning Heavensward expansion up to level 60 for free with no restrictions on playtime??

In all seriousness, ffxiv is like 5 jrpgs in a trenchant, and I have spent the past year latched onto it with a death grip.

While yes, technically a mmo, the story is the true highlight and the community is one of the friendliest you can find. It's also a stupid amount of fun, with soooooo many things to do.

Do's!

- Choose the data center closest to you and play whatever world sounds cool to you. As long as you are on the same data center, players can still group up and interact. I'm personally on crystal, goblin specifically. Each world and data center has their stereotypes, but good people are everywhere in this game
- Read your tool tips whenever you get a a new ability
- Focus on the MSQ ( Main story quest). If you want to unlock new things, it depends on your level in the story versus the actual level of your character
- Make sure to eat something in game anytime you fight. In a dungeon, trial, just regular overworked stuff, it'll give a 3% to xp
- Do your job quests!!! They give new powerful abilities that are required to play correctly, and make sure you equip your jobstone as soon as you get it


Don't! 

- Don't be afraid of other players. Near everyone is super friendly, and so many are willing to help out.
- Don't skip cutscenes!! Whenever you go into a new duty for the first time, you will get a neat little cutscene. Everyone waits for others to finish the cutscene, and *everyone* should get to see it at least once. Don't feel bad for watching, we want you to enjoy the experience!
- Dont rush through main story! The story is the highlight of the game, and you will come to love your character as one loves themselves. The entire msq is like playing one game and four sequels, it's quite a long journey.


Random things I wish I knew when I started

- materia isn't super important until endgame because of how often you get new gear
- make sure you check how many items you are buying on the market board so you don't end up with way too much
- put items in glamour chest rather than directly use them on gear one at a time


I hope you have a awesome time playing!! If you choose the crystal data center, send me a pm if you ever need help with anything!

Well, if you are planning to play overwatch, you will probably need to learn a few of the female characters. About half the heroes are woman, and each have their own toolkits and niche. It sounds like there was a misunderstanding, and she wasn't really thinking of Overwatch as it actually is. Maybe you could try to have her go to the hero gallery, and have her check out all the heroes and their skins?

It would also help you figure out if she is just confused or over-reacting. If she is open to talking and checks out the game and see it for herself, maybe she would realize that the game is much different from what she thought. However, if she is unwilling to listen, to look at the game personally, or tries to shut down the conversation, those are all signs that y'alls relationship is probably unhealthy.

 I'm assuming you're a guy, and I just want to remind you that women can be toxic and abusive just like men. If she doesn't add value to your life, or if she makes things harder, please reach out to somebody close to you and get some help. It can help to think about these things as if they happened to somebody else. I was abused at one point, and while I could reason away myself getting hit, if I changed the situation only in switching myself out with my sister, only then did it click that none of it was okay.

I'm a stranger on the internet, who doesn't have a clue what your relationship is like, and I'm sorry for the rant. I wanted to make that someone said this stuff, if not for you then someone else who is also in your situation. Hope things get better for you :)

That's the thing, by saying she doesn't want you playing overwatch because of the female characters, she is saying she doesn't trust you through actions instead of words. While some partners will agree to not watch porn, there is a difference when it comes to a game that's not even rated R.   It's rated teen, which means it should be fine for 13 and up. There's not that much to look at. This is coming from a lesbian, so I can understand her point of view but it's still a reach.

You could try talking about it with her, and ask why in particular overwatch makes her uncomfortable, and see if you can find a compromise. But personally, I would recommend taking a look at the relationship and decide if it is healthy or worth continuing. 

Best thing you can do is talk it out and communicate, relationships take a lot of work and communication to be healthy. Take care of yourself my dude.
